title: Private Deployments — VPC & On‑Prem Reference, Packaging, Day‑2 Ops, Upgrades and Customer Requirements
author: Priya Natarajan
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical reference for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem). It consolidates the recommended reference architectures, network and packaging requirements, day‑2 operational guidance, and standardized upgrade and rollback procedures. Use this page as the primary handoff to customer SRE/Platform teams and solutions engineers.

Sections included:
- Introduction and scope
- Ownership and escalation
- VPC reference architecture (production)
- On‑prem reference architecture and packaging model
- Day‑2 operations: monitoring, backups, capacity, security
- Upgrade and rollback playbook (canary + automated validation)
- Customer requirements library (checklist and templates)
- Appendix: example manifests, commands, and test checklist

1) Introduction and scope

This guide covers Redwood Private: fully managed control plane with customer VPC peering and the on‑prem installer option (air‑gapped or connected). It applies to customer environments that require data residency, network isolation, or compliance controls. For Hosted API or Redwood Dedicated flows, see product docs; this doc focuses on private deployment concerns.

2) Ownership and escalation

Primary owners:
- Eng Private Deployments (team owner): eng-private-deployments@redwood.internal
- Solutions Engineering: sol-eng@redwood.internal (pre-sale, onboarding)
- Customer Success (post-sale adoption): cs@redwood.internal

Escalation matrix:
1. Customer reports issue -> Solutions Engineer or CS creates issue in Jira (project: PRIVATE-OPS)
2. Oncall rotation for eng-private-deployments responds within 30 minutes for P1
3. If not resolved in 2 hours, escalate to Eng Platform lead and SRE manager

3) VPC reference architecture (production)

Goals: minimal blast radius, predictable latency to customer services, strong audit trails.

High-level topology (textual diagram):
- Customer VPC A (private subnets) <-> Transit & Peering -> Redwood Private Control Plane (managed by Redwood in customer account or via cross-account role)
- Optional: PrivateLink or AWS Transit Gateway for multi-region connectivity

Network components and requirements table:
| Component | Requirement | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subnets | At least 2 private subnets per AZ | /24 recommended per subnet for autoscaling headroom |
| NAT | Outbound NAT for installer artifacts (unless air-gapped) | Use NAT Gateway for high throughput |
| Security groups | Restrictive by default; allow only necessary ports | See port table below |
| DNS | Private hosted zone for internal service discovery | Recommend Route53 private hosted zone |

Port table (minimum):
- TCP 443: control plane API and telemetry (egress/ingress rules as configured)
- TCP 22: optional SSH for debug (restricted to customer admin CIDRs)
- TCP 9100-9200: metrics and exporter endpoints (customer can restrict)
- TCP 61616, 9092: only if customer enables legacy connectors

Identity and access:
- Use cross-account IAM roles with least privilege for Redwood-managed control plane actions; include explicit STS assume role TTL of 1 hour
- Customer must provide KMS key ARN for envelope encryption of persistent secrets

4) On‑prem reference architecture and packaging model

Packaging options:
- Installer image (OCI) + Helm charts for Kubernetes-based installs (recommended)
- Binary tarball plus systemd units for bare-metal references (air-gapped)
- Appliance ISO for fully isolated environments (partner-managed)

Minimum node sizing (Kubernetes):
- Control plane components: 3 nodes, 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM, 200 GB NVMe each (HA)
- GPU inference workers (if customer brings GPUs): match model memory requirements + 20% headroom; recommended instance types: A100-40GB / H100-80GB variants or equivalent vendor HW

Packaging checklist (on‑prem Helm):
- Values file contains: imagePullPolicy, registry.mirror, storageClass, nodeSelector, tolerations, resourceRequests/limits, kmsKeyARN placeholder
- Operator CRDs applied in order: kms-secrets, telemetry, router, api-server, scheduler

Example values snippet (Helm, stylized):
```
image:
  registry: registry.redwood.example.com/mirror
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
storage:
  class: fast-ssd
  size: 500Gi
network:
  podCIDR: 10.244.0.0/16
  serviceCIDR: 10.96.0.0/12
```

5) Day‑2 operations

Monitoring and alerting:
- Required telemetry: Prometheus metrics, node exporter, application traces (OTEL), and structured logs to customer SIEM or S3 bucket
- Default alerts (examples):
  - Control plane API error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes -> P2
  - Scheduler backlog > 3000 requests -> P1
  - KV cache miss rate increase > 10% baseline -> P2
  - Node disk utilization > 75% -> P1

Backups and restore:
- Customer must enable periodic etcd/metadata backups (recommendation: daily full snapshot, hourly incremental)
- Store backups to customer-controlled S3 or NFS; encryption using customer KMS
- Restore playbook: verify snapshot integrity, bring up control plane in DR namespace, run smoke tests (see Appendix)

Capacity planning and autoscaling:
- Baseline sizing should target 95th percentile token throughput with 20% headroom
- Recommend autoscaling policy for worker pools: min=2, target-cpu=60%, max based on committed capacity

Security and compliance:
- Enforce TLS mutual auth for control plane components when supported
- Audit logging: forward API and infra audit events to customer SIEM with 90 day retention by default

6) Upgrade and rollback playbook (stable release process)

Goals: safe canary, automated validation, predictable rollback. Use release tags compatible with customer pinned versions.

Pre-upgrade checklist (run by SE + customer infra):
1. Verify backups: latest snapshot < 2 hours old
2. Confirm health: all control plane pods at Ready, control API 200 OK, scheduler backlog < 100
3. Confirm capacity: at least 20% spare CPU/memory across nodes
4. Confirm maintenance window and stakeholder contact list

Canary upgrade steps (example):
1. Push Helm chart to staging registry and tag release (vX.Y.Z-canary)
2. Deploy to single AZ or single canary node pool with strategy: maxUnavailable=0, maxSurge=1
3. Run automated smoke tests (5-10 sample requests including long context, streaming, and embeddings)
4. Monitor metrics for 30 minutes: error rate, p50/p95 latency, KV cache hit rate, tail latency. Abort if any threshold crossed:
   - error rate increases > 0.5% absolute
   - p95 latency increases > 20% relative
5. If canary passes, rollout to remaining nodes with rolling upgrade (75 minute window per AZ recommended)

Automated validation commands (examples):
- smoke test script: ./scripts/smoke-test.sh --endpoint https://private-api.customer.local --count 20
- metrics query (PromQL): rate(redwood_api_errors_total[5m]) / rate(redwood_api_requests_total[5m])

Rollback procedure:
1. If canary fails, immediately revert Helm release to previous chart: helm rollback <release> 1
2. Re-run smoke tests against rollback state
3. Open postmortem and block future rollouts for that chart minor version until root cause triaged

7) Customer requirements library (checklist and templates)

This section is the canonical checklist used during sales and onboarding. Provide completed checklist to solutions engineering for configuration.

Minimum customer-provided items:
- Network: dedicated VPC ID, list of subnets, admin CIDR allowlist for SSH and control plane access
- IAM: role ARN for Redwood cross-account operations (if applicable) and service principal details
- KMS: customer-managed KMS key ARN for secret envelope encryption
- Storage: bucket name (S3/GCS) for backups and telemetry export with write policy
- Compliance: SOC2 / ISO controls owner and required retention periods for logs and metrics

Customer readiness checklist (to be completed in onboarding):
1. Network connectivity validation completed (ping, TLS handshake, egress rules)
2. Infrastructure quotas validated (IP addresses, ENIs, volumes)
3. Test workload executed and performance validated (sample prompt tests)
4. Backup and restore tested and documented
5. Handed over runbooks and oncall rotation

Templates included in repository:
- Helm values template: templates/helm/values.template.yaml
- Network diagram template: templates/diagrams/vpc-reference.drawio
- Onboarding checklist CSV: templates/onboarding/checklist.csv

8) Appendix: smoke tests and manual commands

Smoke test checklist (manual):
- API health: curl -k https://private-api.local/health -> 200 and JSON {status: ok}
- Authentication: perform a token request and run a small completion and embedding call
- Latency: record p50/p95 over 100 requests (long and short prompts)
- Persistence: create and retrieve a sample KV cache item (if enabled)

Example restore command (etcd snapshot):
- etcdctl snapshot restore /backups/snapshot.db --name redwood-restore --data-dir /var/lib/etcd-restored
